question.leadin: This general's "neckties" were formed using railroad rails he destroyed in one campaign.
question.text: Name this general, who made use of scorched earth tactics in his "March to the Sea".
question.clue: This military leader issued "Special Field Orders Number 15," demanding parcels of 40 acres be given to freed slaves.

swap.leadin: The repulsion of Pickett's Charge at Cemetery Ridge secured victory in this battle for Union forces.
swap.text: Identify this pivotal battle of the Civil War in Pennsylvania, where Joshua Chamberlain led Union forces in a downhill bayonet charge at Little Round Top.
swap.clue: During this battle, Joshua Chamberlain led a bayonet charge of the 20th Maine that secured Little Round Top.

question.text: This former president was that only presidential candidate.
question.clue: He appointed Brigham Young as first territorial governor of Utah, which led to the first territorial capital being named after this president.

swap.text: Douglass published this anti-slavery newspaper from 1847-1851. The newspaper is named after a celestial object that many slaves used as a guide while escaping to freedom.
swap.clue: Inspired by William Lloyd Garrison's The Liberator, Douglass started this newspaper in 1847.

question.leadin: William Henry Seward's "Higher Law" speech opposed it.
question.text: Name this compromise which admitted California into the Union as a free state in exchange for a national Fugitive Slave Act.
question.clue: Texas agreed to place its northern border at 36o30' and relinquished its claims to New Mexico.

swap.leadin: Douglas S. Freeman received a 1935 Pulitzer Prize for a four-volume biography of this person.
swap.text: Name this general, whose "Lieutenants" title a Douglas Freeman book about subordinate officers in the Army of Northern Virginia.
swap.clue: That subordinate was mortally wounded in another battle at a low stone wall called "the angle," sometimes called the "high-water mark" of this commander's cause.

question.leadin: After the Wisconsin Supreme Court ruled this legislation unconstitutional, the Supreme Court ruled in Ableman vs. Booth that state courts cannot issue rulings contradicting federal court decisions.
question.text: Name this legislation included in the Compromise of 1850 that strengthened a 1793 legislation of the same name. Several states passed personal liberty laws to protect victims of this legislation.
question.clue: The Wisconsin Supreme Court declared this law unconstitutional, a decision ultimately rejected in the Supreme Court case Ableman v. Booth.

swap.text: Grant had earlier won this siege of a major Mississippi River city, which occurred a day after the Battle of Gettysburg.
swap.clue: The losing side of this battle was unable to stop enemy advances at Champion Hill and Big Black River Bridge.

question.leadin: One hundred and twenty members of the Baker-Fancher party were murdered on their way from Arkansas to California.
question.text: Name this massacre that occurred in 1857 on the Old Spanish Trail.
question.clue: During this event, a militia dressed up as Paiute ] Indians killed members of the Baker-Fancher wagon train.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a Civil War battle.
swap.text: On July 21, 1861, Union forces under Irwin McDowell were soundly defeated by the Confederates at this battle, where Thomas Jackson earned the nickname "Stonewall."
swap.answerHtml: First Battle of Bull Run [accept First Battle of Manassas; prompt on Bull Run; prompt on Manassas]
swap.clue: The high civilian turnout at this battle granted it its nickname of a "picnic battle."

question.text: This Confederate was appointed as commander of the Army of Tennessee over Joseph Johnston in 1864; he then rather unsuccessfully conducted the Atlanta campaign against Sherman and lost to George Thomas at Nashville.
question.clue: His rapid attacks saved the Southern army from severe defeat first at South Mountain and then at Antietam, after which he as promoted the army's youngest major general.

swap.text: This man, who led the Army of the Potomac, commanded the Union forces at Gettysburg. Lincoln criticized him for not actively pursuing Lee into Virginia.
swap.clue: During his feud with Daniel Sickles, who nearly cost him his most famous victory, this man was accused of inactivity similar to that he showed at Mine Run.

question.leadin: Even though he was on trial for murder, Vice President Aaron Burr still presided over the impeachment of a politician with this last name.
question.text: Give this surname of the first Supreme Court justice to be impeached. A different politician with this last name presided over Texas v. White as Chief Justice in the aftermath of the American Civil War.
question.clue: A man with this last name added "In God We Trust" on coinage and succeeded Roger Taney's post after Taney's death.

swap.text: An anarchist named Alexander Berkman tried to assassinate Henry Clay Frick, Carnegie's right-hand man, during a strike in this Pennsylvania steel town which Frick had tried to break using hundreds of Pinkertons.
swap.clue: Because he believed the Red River Valley needed large-scale irrigation, John Wesley Powell encouraged settlers to establish bonanza farms instead of these family owned farms that were given to settlers by an 1862 act.

question.leadin: This historian won the 1940 Pulitzer Prize for History for the second part of a biography divided into The Prairie Years and The War Years.
question.text: Name this historian and poet who wrote the six-volume biography Abraham Lincoln. Those books by this historian inspired Robert Sherwood's play Abe Lincoln in Illinois.

swap.leadin: Clarina Nichols lobbied to ensure a guarantee for property rights and limited voting for women in this document.
swap.text: Name this 1859 constitution, under which Kansas joined the U.S. as a free state.

question.leadin: This politician was dubbed "the Lion of White Hall" in reference to his family home in Kentucky, where he founded the abolitionist newspaper True American in Lexington in 1845.
question.text: Name this Kentucky planter who was named Minister to Russia by Abraham Lincoln at the very start of the Civil War, in which role he drummed up Russian support for the Union.
question.clue: He resigned his generalship in the Union Army when Lincoln would not immediately emancipate all slaves.

swap.leadin: In a letter to general William Rosecrans, President Lincoln described this battle as a "hard victory which, had there been a defeat instead, the nation could scarcely have lived over."
swap.text: Name this Civil War battle that began on December 31, 1862, in central Tennessee, where Rosecrans forced the Army of the Tennessee to withdraw. After the first day of this battle, George Thomas declared he knew of "no better place to die" to persuade Rosecrans not to retreat.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Stones River [or the Second Battle of Murfreesboro]
swap.clue: In an earlier battle, Bragg had retreated from Perryville to this site in Tennessee and here he first went up against Rosecrans on December 31, 1862. Bragg again retreated, this time to Tullahoma, creating a nine-month stalemate on the front.

question.leadin: This ship's captain wrote the book Memoirs of Service Afloat During the War Between the States.
question.text: Name this Confederate raider, built in Britain and captained by Raphael Semmes, which was sunk by the U.S.S. Kearsarge off the coast of France in 1864.
question.clue: Its namesake "claims" awarded over fifteen million dollars, ruling that the country which built it was responsible for its actions.

swap.text: During the Civil War, she was appointed superintendent of female nurses to the Union army, but made her name in the antebellum era as a crusader for the reform of prisons and mental health institutions.
swap.clue: This woman served as the Superintendent of Union Army nurses during the Civil War, though she is more famous for inspiring the creation of institutions such as Harrisburg State Hospital.
